title: Observability conduit: federated hookset and tenant healthboard for Dedicated & Private
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Ship a federated observability conduit that provides a reusable set of tracing hooks (hookset) and a tenant-scoped healthboard for Dedicated and Private deployments. Motivation: customers using VPC/on-prem collectors require per-tenant latency/error visibility, consistent trace context propagation across relay boundaries, and safe fallbacks when collector pipelines are backpressured or misbehaving. This ticket covers: 1) a lightweight hookset library for inject/extract and canonical tenant-mapping semantics (opaque headers, signed tenant envelope), 2) collector-side adapters that translate hookset headers into internal span/metric labels, and 3) a Grafana-based "Tenant Healthboard" view that surfaces SLO regressions, top error traces, and per-tenant ingestion lag for Dedicated & Private clusters.
acceptance_criteria: Hookset library published (go/py) with docs and examples for private customers
Collector adapter implemented to attach tenant_id and route_reason to spans and metrics
Healthboard dashboard deployed in staging showing per-tenant P95 latency, 4xx/5xx rates, and ingestion lag with data from on-prem collectors
Automated tests for header signing/verification and collector backpressure handling
Canary rollout plan for Dedicated fleets with rollback criteria defined

implementation_notes: Hookset API: minimal surface - Inject(context, tenant_meta) and Extract(headers) with signature verification path
Collector Adapter: pipeline stage 'tenant-enrich' to run before span-batching; emit metric rw.collector.enrich.latency and rw.collector.enrich.failures
Backpressure strategy: if adapter queue > 85% or enrichment error rate > 1%, mark spans with enrich_status=degraded and emit a telemetry counter for remediation
Dashboard: backend uses tenant-aggregates stored in nosql timeseries (TTL 90d); UI supports subscription-based alerts per tenant
Rollout: start 2-node canary on Dedicated, monitor enrich fail-rate and ingestion-lag, follow with 24h burn-in before wider Dedicated rollout.
